racesCard.region: Screen-reader name of the card for the scheduled online races (they start every few minutes).
racesCard.description: Line under the circuit name of the scheduled races card. {car}: car name, not translated. {laps}: the race's lap count; the English always says 'laps', give your language's plural forms. {interval}: time between races, already formatted, e.g. '10 min' or '90 s'.
racesCard.racing: Big countdown spot while a race is running: 'Go' shown large, 'in progress' small beside it. Keep the <big></big> and <small></small> tags; they style each part.
racesCard.toStart: Countdown to the start of the race you entered. {time}: e.g. '3:45', shown large. Keep the <big></big> and <small></small> tags.
racesCard.toNextRace: Countdown to the next scheduled race. {time}: e.g. '3:45', shown large. Keep the <big></big> and <small></small> tags.
racesCard.entrants: Screen-reader name of the list of drivers in the race you entered.
racesCard.entered: You have joined the next scheduled race; it starts by itself.
racesCard.enteredAlone: You have joined the next scheduled race and nobody else has yet: AI cars fill the grid if no one joins.
racesCard.rules: Rules of the scheduled races: everyone drives the same car, and the starting order comes from each driver's best lap in the weekly challenge.
racesCard.nobodyWaiting: Nobody has joined the next scheduled race yet.
racesCard.waiting: How many drivers have joined the next race. Keep the tags; they bold the text.
racesCard.waitingNames: How many drivers have joined the next race, then their names. {names}: up to three driver names, comma-separated. Keep the tags.
racesCard.waitingNamesMore: As the line with names, plus how many more drivers are waiting beyond the three named. {more}: that number.
racesCard.topDrivers: Heading: the drivers with the most scheduled-race wins this week.
racesCard.winsPodiums: A driver's wins and podium finishes (top three) this week.
racesCard.record: Your own scheduled-race record: races started, wins, podium finishes (top three).
racesCard.recordBest: As the record line, plus your best finishing position. P{best} is racing notation for a position, e.g. P2 = second place.
seatPanel.dialog: Screen-reader name of the seat and camera panel. {car}: the car's name, not translated.
seatPanel.title: Panel title: move the driver's view inside the car and set its field of view.
seatPanel.rows.view: Row label: which in-car camera (cockpit or dash) the panel adjusts.
seatPanel.rows.viewLess: Button: switch to the cockpit camera (the driver's eye).
seatPanel.rows.viewMore: Button: switch to the dash camera (on the dashboard).
seatPanel.rows.fwd: Row label: the view's position forward and back.
seatPanel.rows.right: Row label: the view's position left and right.
seatPanel.rows.tilt: Row label: the view's pitch, looking up or down.
seatPanel.rows.fov: Row label: field of view, how wide the camera sees. FOV is the usual abbreviation; keep it if your language uses it.
seatPanel.rows.fovLess: Button: make the field of view narrower.
seatPanel.rows.fovMore: Button: make the field of view wider.
seatPanel.viewGroup: Screen-reader name of the cockpit / dash camera switch.
seatPanel.resetView: Button: put every seat setting back to the car's default.
seatPanel.prompts.row: Button prompt at the panel's foot: up and down pick a row.
seatPanel.prompts.change: Button prompt: left and right change the picked row.
seatPanel.prompts.resetRow: Button prompt: put the picked row back to the default.
seatPanel.prompts.resetView: Button prompt: put every seat setting back to the default.
seatPanel.savedPerCar: The seat settings are remembered separately for each car.
leaderboardPanel.raceGhost: Screen-reader name of the button that races a replay (ghost) of one of your saved laps. {car}: car name, not translated.
leaderboardPanel.raceGhostTitle: Tooltip of the button that races a replay (ghost car) of a lap.
leaderboardPanel.postUnreachable: Shown when a lap couldn't be sent to the online lap board because the server didn't answer.
leaderboardPanel.applySetup: Screen-reader name of the button that loads the car setup saved with one of your laps. {car}: car name, not translated.
leaderboardPanel.applySetupTitle: Tooltip of the button that loads a lap's car setup.
leaderboardPanel.retry: Button: send a lap to the online board again after it failed.
leaderboardPanel.post: Button: send a lap to the online lap board.
leaderboardPanel.retryAria: Screen-reader name of the narrow-screen retry button.
leaderboardPanel.postAria: Screen-reader name of the narrow-screen post button.
leaderboardPanel.retryTitle: Tooltip of the narrow-screen retry button.
leaderboardPanel.postTitle: Tooltip of the narrow-screen post button.
leaderboardPanel.notPosted: Under a lap that failed to reach the online board. {error}: the server's reason, in English.
leaderboardPanel.driverKey: Heading. A driver key is a small file that proves you own your driver name on the online board.
leaderboardPanel.importGhost: Button: load a lap replay (ghost) from a file to race against.
leaderboardPanel.exportBest: Button: save your best lap's replay (ghost) to a file.
leaderboardPanel.onlineTimes: Title of the online lap board.
leaderboardPanel.circuitLaps: Number of your saved laps on a circuit, shown in the circuit picker.
leaderboardPanel.carLaps: Number of your saved laps in a car, shown in the car picker.
leaderboardPanel.physicsVersion: Screen-reader name of the picker for lap boards of older physics versions (laps are only compared within one version).
leaderboardPanel.car: Screen-reader name of the car picker.
leaderboardPanel.noLapsOlder: {circuit}: circuit name, not translated. {board}: name of an older physics version's board, e.g. 'Physics v7'.
leaderboardPanel.tableLabel: Screen-reader name of the table of your best laps. {circuit}: circuit name, not translated.
leaderboardPanel.carColumn: Column header of the car name in your best laps table.
leaderboardPanel.theoreticalBest: Your best three sectors (parts of the lap) added together: the fastest lap you could do.
leaderboardPanel.potential: Time your best lap could gain if it had your best sectors. {delta}: e.g. '−0.412'; s = seconds.
leaderboardPanel.allBestSectors: Your best lap already holds your best time in every sector.
leaderboardPanel.signIn: Button next to Export key and Import key, shown only while signed out: opens Settings > Profile and data > Account.
leaderboardPanel.signInHint: Hint under those buttons, shown only while signed out: an account carries best laps and driver names to every device, so the driver key file needn't be moved by hand.
boardWidget.modes.lapEnd: When the lap board opens by itself: for a few seconds after each lap.
boardWidget.modes.open: When the lap board opens by itself: it stays open.
boardWidget.modes.closed: When the lap board opens by itself: never (only by its key or a click).
boardWidget.gear: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the small gear button on the lap board, which opens the menu of the three options.
boardWidget.modeMenu: Screen-reader name of the menu with the three opening options.
boardWidget.region: Screen-reader name of the lap board shown while driving (your place on the circuit's online lap times).
boardWidget.fold: Screen-reader name of the lap board's header button, which folds it to one line.
boardWidget.foldKey: As 'Fold the lap board', with the key that does it. {key}: a key name such as J.
boardWidget.open: Screen-reader name of the folded lap board. {circuit}: circuit name. {place}: your place, e.g. 'P14/312' (14th of 312).
boardWidget.openNoTime: Screen-reader name of the folded lap board when you have no time on it yet. {circuit}: circuit name.
boardWidget.openKey: As the open line, with the key that opens it. {key}: a key name such as J.
boardWidget.openKeyNoTime: As the no-time line, with the key that opens it. {key}: a key name such as J.
boardWidget.drivers: How many drivers have a time on this board. {count}: the number, already formatted (e.g. 1,284).
boardWidget.placesBetween: Screen-reader name of the gap row standing for the places not shown between two parts of the list.
boardWidget.lapsDriven: Small label at the board's foot: how many laps everyone has driven on this circuit in this car.
boardWidget.noTime: Shown in place of your position when you have no lap on this board yet.
multiplayerPanel.collision.on: Collision setting of an online room: cars touch each other.
multiplayerPanel.collision.ghostLap1: Collision setting: cars pass through each other (ghosted) on the first lap only.
multiplayerPanel.collision.off: Collision setting: cars always pass through each other.
multiplayerPanel.collision.protected: Collision setting of public races: ghosted on lap 1, then a car driving dangerously can't touch others.
multiplayerPanel.anyCar: Car rule of a room: drivers may pick any car.
multiplayerPanel.startType.standing: Race start type: from a standstill on the grid.
multiplayerPanel.startType.rolling: Race start type: the field is already moving when the race starts.
multiplayerPanel.gridOrder.qualifying: Grid order: by qualifying lap times.
multiplayerPanel.gridOrder.reverse: Grid order: qualifying order reversed (fastest at the back).
multiplayerPanel.gridOrderHint.qualifyin: Hint for the qualifying grid order: fastest lap starts first; drivers without a time line up in the order they joined.
multiplayerPanel.gridOrderHint.random: Hint for the random grid order: drawn when the race starts.
multiplayerPanel.presetClassic: Race rules preset: the original online rules (track-limit strikes).
multiplayerPanel.presetClassicHint: Track limits: every third time a driver leaves the track adds a time penalty, first 3 seconds, later 5. s = seconds.
multiplayerPanel.timeScaleFixed: Time speed setting: the time of day doesn't move.
multiplayerPanel.settings.event: Card title: the race's circuit, cars and conditions.
multiplayerPanel.settings.race: Card title: laps, qualifying, grid and start.
multiplayerPanel.settings.rules: Card title: the race rules (track limits, penalties, damage, collisions).
multiplayerPanel.settings.changeCircuit: Screen-reader name of the Change button. {circuit}: circuit name, not translated.
multiplayerPanel.settings.change: Button: pick another circuit for the room.
multiplayerPanel.settings.circuitHint: Only the room's host can change the circuit, from the main menu.
multiplayerPanel.settings.cars: Row label: which cars the room allows.
multiplayerPanel.settings.oneCar: Hint: everyone in the room drives the same car.
multiplayerPanel.settings.classesMixed: Hint: any car is allowed, so cars of different classes race together.
multiplayerPanel.settings.timeSpeed: Row label: how fast the time of day moves during the race.
multiplayerPanel.settings.qualifying: Row label: length of the qualifying session before the race.
multiplayerPanel.settings.qualifyingHint: Each driver's best lap without track-limit offences decides the starting order.
multiplayerPanel.settings.setByQualifyin: Value of Grid order when the room runs qualifying.
multiplayerPanel.settings.start: Row label: standing or rolling start.
multiplayerPanel.settings.launch: Row label: whether the start is assisted or the driver controls clutch and throttle.
multiplayerPanel.settings.rulePreset: Row label: the race rules preset.
multiplayerPanel.settings.penaltiesOn: Value of the Penalties row: time penalties are given.
multiplayerPanel.settings.penaltiesOff: Value of the Penalties row: no time penalties.
multiplayerPanel.settings.penaltiesHint: Penalty seconds are added for leaving the track and for jumping the start.
multiplayerPanel.settings.damage: Row label: how much damage cars take.
multiplayerPanel.settings.lockedQualifyi: Under the Event card: the host can't change settings during qualifying.
multiplayerPanel.settings.lockedRace: Under the Event card: the host can't change settings during the race.
multiplayerPanel.net.relayedTitle: Tooltip: this player's connection goes through the host instead of directly.
multiplayerPanel.net.relayed: Badge: the connection is relayed through the host.
multiplayerPanel.net.measuring: Badge: the connection's ping is still being measured.
multiplayerPanel.net.pingLoss: Connection quality badge. {ping}: round-trip time in milliseconds (ms). {loss}: percent of packets lost.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.title: Card title: the drivers in the room.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.host: Who hosts the room. {name}: a driver name.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.qualifying: Badge: the qualifying session is running.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.noCar: A driver in the room hasn't picked a car yet.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.noTime: Badge during qualifying: the driver has no lap time yet.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.wrongClassTitle: Tooltip of the Wrong class badge. {class}: the room's car class, e.g. GT3 or 'Any car'.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.wrongClass: Badge: the driver's car isn't allowed in this room.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.ready: Badge beside a driver: ready to race.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.notReady: Badge beside a driver: not ready yet.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.hostOn: Warning: the host's race is on another circuit than the one you have loaded. {circuit}: circuit name.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.wrongCar: Warning to you. {class}: the room's car class.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.wrongCarSwitch: Warning to you, followed by buttons naming cars you can switch to. {class}: the room's car class.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.raceInProgress: The host's start button while a race runs (disabled).
multiplayerPanel.drivers.startRaceNow: Host's button during qualifying: end qualifying and start the race.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.startQualifying: Host's button: start the qualifying session. {minutes}: its length in minutes; min = minutes.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.endQualifying: Host's button: stop the qualifying session.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.endRaceForEvery: Host's button: stop the race for every driver.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.readyButton: Guest's button once pressed: you are marked ready (press again to undo).
multiplayerPanel.drivers.readyUp: Guest's button: mark yourself ready to race.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.confirmEndRace: Title of the confirmation before the host ends the race for all drivers.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.confirmEndQuali: Confirm button: end the qualifying session.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.keepQualifying: Cancel button: let qualifying go on.
multiplayerPanel.drivers.keepRacing: Cancel button: let the race go on.
multiplayerPanel.room.connected: Connection badge: how many other players you are connected to.
multiplayerPanel.room.connecting: Connection badge: the connection to the room is being set up.
multiplayerPanel.room.title: Card title: a room you host or join with a code, for racing friends.
multiplayerPanel.room.codeAria: Screen-reader text for the room's code. {code}: e.g. K7Q2XD.
multiplayerPanel.room.codeCaption: Caption under the big room code.
multiplayerPanel.room.linkCopied: Button text for two seconds after the invite link was copied.
multiplayerPanel.room.share: Button: open the device's share sheet with the invite link.
multiplayerPanel.room.host: Button: create a room of your own.
multiplayerPanel.room.joinAnother: Label of the code field when you already host a room.
multiplayerPanel.room.newRoom: Button: host a fresh room with a new code.
multiplayerPanel.room.codeTooShort: Error under the code field: room codes have at least 3 characters.
multiplayerPanel.room.shareTitle: Title of the invite sent through the device's share sheet. LibreCorsa is the game's name, not translated.
multiplayerPanel.room.shareText: Text of the invite sent through the share sheet, followed by the link.
multiplayerPanel.room.racingAs: Screen-reader name of your driver card. {name}: your driver name.
multiplayerPanel.room.edit: Button: edit your driver name, code and colour.
multiplayerPanel.connect.hide: Expander when open: hide the advanced connection methods.
multiplayerPanel.connect.localTitle: Section: race between two browser tabs on this computer.
multiplayerPanel.connect.manualTitle: Section: connect two players by copying codes by hand. WebRTC is a technology name, not translated.
multiplayerPanel.connect.manualIntro: Offer and answer are the two tokens the players swap; keep the technical meaning.
multiplayerPanel.connect.createOffer: Step 1 button, for the host: make a token to send to the guest.
multiplayerPanel.connect.acceptOffer: Step 2 button, for the guest: read the host's token and make an answer token.
multiplayerPanel.connect.acceptAnswer: Step 3 button, for the host: read the guest's answer token.
multiplayerPanel.connect.remoteToken: Field label: the token the other player sent you.
multiplayerPanel.connect.yourToken: Field label: the token to send to the other player.
multiplayerPanel.connect.copied: Button text after the token was copied.
multiplayerPanel.connect.reset: Button: start the manual connection over.
multiplayerPanel.connect.turnTitle: Section: your own relay server. TURN is a technical name, keep it.
multiplayerPanel.connect.turnIntro: A relay passes the race traffic on networks that block direct connections.
multiplayerPanel.connect.relayAddress: Field label: the relay server's address.
multiplayerPanel.connect.username: Field label: the relay server's user name.
multiplayerPanel.connect.password: Field label: the relay server's password.
multiplayerPanel.connect.saved: Button text after the relay settings were saved.
multiplayerPanel.connect.clear: Button: remove the saved relay server.
multiplayerPanel.connect.turnPrefix: Error: the address must begin with 'turn:' or 'turns:'. Keep turn: and turns: as they are.
multiplayerPanel.connect.ownRelay: Your own relay server (set below) is in use.
boardWidget.place: The player's place on the lap board, e.g. P14/312 = 14th of 312 drivers. {rank}: the place. {total}: the number of drivers, already formatted.
pauseMenu.tabs.label: Screen-reader name of the pause menu's tab strip.
pauseMenu.tabs.session: Pause menu tab: camera and the race's rules for this session.
pauseMenu.tabs.hud: Pause menu tab: pick the on-screen display layout. HUD = head-up display; usually kept as HUD.
pauseMenu.tabs.conditions: Pause menu tab: weather and time of day.
pauseMenu.tabs.garage: Pause menu tab: car setup (tyres, wings, suspension).
pauseMenu.tabs.corners: Pause menu tab: a map of the circuit's corners; picking one puts the car there.
pauseMenu.tabs.lapTimes: Pause menu tab: lap time boards.
pauseMenu.tabs.feedback: Pause menu tab: send a bug report, a request or an idea.
pauseMenu.actions.label: Screen-reader name of the pause menu's list of actions.
pauseMenu.actions.resume: Pause menu: go back to driving.
pauseMenu.actions.restartRace: Pause menu: start the race again from the grid.
pauseMenu.actions.gridStart: Pause menu (practice, no AI cars): restart from a standing start on the grid.
pauseMenu.actions.rollingStart: Pause menu (race against AI): restart the race with a rolling start (the field already moving).
pauseMenu.actions.flyingLap: Pause menu (practice): restart already at speed, so the first lap is a timed one.
pauseMenu.actions.skipTrack: Pause menu: skip to the next music track.
pauseMenu.actions.nowPlaying: Line under Skip track: the music playing. {title}: track title; {composer}: its composer. Neither is translated.
pauseMenu.actions.mainMenu: Pause menu: leave the session for the title screen.
pauseMenu.prompts.move: Button prompt at the bottom of the screen: the stick or arrow keys move the cursor.
pauseMenu.prompts.select: Button prompt: confirm the highlighted item.
pauseMenu.prompts.jumpThere: Button prompt on the Corners tab: put the car at the highlighted corner.
pauseMenu.prompts.tabs: Button prompt: shoulder buttons switch between tabs.
pauseMenu.prompts.page: Button prompt: triggers turn the board's pages.
pauseMenu.prompts.back: Button prompt: step back (a panel, then the tabs, then the menu).
pauseMenu.prompts.resume: Button prompt: close the pause menu and drive on.
pauseMenu.header.lap: Under the circuit name: the lap the car is on. {lap}: a number.
pauseMenu.header.lapOf: Under the circuit name in a race: the lap the car is on out of the race's laps, e.g. 'Lap 3/10'.
pauseMenu.header.run: Under the circuit name on a hill climb: the number of the timed run (start to finish), not a lap.
pauseMenu.header.position: Race position out of the number of cars, e.g. 'P3/12'. P = position; keep the short form your language's motorsport coverage uses.
pauseMenu.header.online: Badge: this is an online race with other players.
pauseMenu.header.leavesRace: Shown when a new version is ready: reloading now leaves the online race.
pauseMenu.header.leavesRoom: Shown when a new version is ready: reloading now leaves the online room (lobby).
pauseMenu.header.endsSession: Shown when a new version is ready: reloading now ends this driving session.
pauseMenu.session.title: Card title on the Session tab when there are no race rules to show.
pauseMenu.session.autopilot: Switch: the computer drives the player's car.
pauseMenu.session.key: Hint beside a switch. {key}: a keyboard key name such as P, not translated.
pauseMenu.session.cameraView: Setting: which camera view the car is driven from (chase, cockpit…).
pauseMenu.session.cycle: Hint: the key that steps through the camera views. {key}: a key name such as C.
pauseMenu.session.freeCamera: Setting row: a camera the player flies freely around the circuit.
pauseMenu.session.freeCameraHint: {key}: a key name such as F7. Drag the mouse to look, WASD keys to fly, Q and E to go down and up. Keep WASD and Q/E as they are.
pauseMenu.session.freeCameraButton: Button that switches to the free camera.
pauseMenu.session.exitFreeCamera: Button that leaves the free camera. Short: it sits in a small button.
pauseMenu.session.tv: Setting row: TV-style cameras placed beside the track, as on a race broadcast.
pauseMenu.session.tvHint: {key}: a key name such as F8.
pauseMenu.session.tvButton: Button that switches to the trackside TV cameras.
pauseMenu.session.exitTv: Button that leaves the trackside TV cameras. Short: it sits in a small button.
pauseMenu.hud.title: Card title: the on-screen display layout. HUD = head-up display.
pauseMenu.hud.settings: Button opening the HUD part of Settings.
pauseMenu.corners.title: Card title on the Corners tab.
pauseMenu.corners.mapLabel: Screen-reader description of the circuit map.
pauseMenu.corners.turn: Short corner name on the map and list, e.g. 'T4' for turn 4. Keep it short.
pauseMenu.corners.detail: {complex}: the name of the group of corners (not translated). {sector}: the timing sector number (1-3).
pauseMenu.corners.pick: Hint shown until a corner is highlighted.
pauseMenu.corners.rowLabel: Screen-reader name of a corner button. {name}, {complex}: corner names, not translated. {apex}: lowest speed through the corner; {unit}: km/h or mph; {gear}: the gear used.
pauseMenu.corners.gear: The gear used through the corner. Keep the <n></n> tags around the number; they style it.
lapSummary.title: The lap's name. {kind}: 'run' on a hill climb (one timed run from start to finish), else 'lap'. {lap}: its number.
lapSummary.open: Screen-reader name of the lap toast: pressing it opens the lap's details. {kind} and {lap} as in the title.
lapSummary.dismiss: Screen-reader name of the close button on the small after-lap card.
lapSummary.collapse: Screen-reader name of the button that folds the lap details back into the small card.
lapSummary.cardLabel: Screen-reader name of the lap details panel. {lap}: the lap number.
lapSummary.invalid: Badge: the lap broke the track limits and doesn't count.
lapSummary.pb: Badge: personal best lap. Short form; keep it 2-3 letters.
lapSummary.invalidWall: Badge: the lap doesn't count because the car hit a wall.
lapSummary.invalidLimits: Badge: the lap doesn't count because the car left the track.
lapSummary.autopilot: Badge: the computer drove part of the lap, so it isn't put on the online board.
lapSummary.online: Badge: the lap went up to the online board.
lapSummary.onlineRank: Badge: the lap's place on the online board. P = position. {rank}: a number.
lapSummary.onlineRankOf: Badge: the lap's place on the online board out of {total} drivers.
lapSummary.onlineRankWeek: Badge: board place, then the place in this week's challenge ({week}).
lapSummary.onlineRankOfWeek: Badge: board place out of {total} drivers, then the place in this week's challenge ({week}).
lapSummary.invalidUnranked: Why the lap can't go online: it was invalid.
lapSummary.autopilotUnranked: Why the lap can't go online: the computer drove.
lapSummary.topSpeed: Stat label under a number: the lap's top speed. {unit}: km/h or mph.
lapSummary.avgSpeed: Stat label under a number: the lap's average speed. {unit}: km/h or mph.
lapSummary.fullThrottle: Stat label under a percentage: share of the lap at full throttle.
lapSummary.braking: Stat label under a percentage: share of the lap spent braking.
lapSummary.sector: A timing sector's label under its time. {n}: 1-3. {mark}: 'best' (session best), 'pb' (personal best), 'slower', or none.
lapSummary.theoreticalBest: The lap time made of the best time in each sector.
lapSummary.posting: Status: the lap is being sent to the online board.
lapSummary.postingNow: Button text while the lap is being sent to the online board.
lapSummary.retry: Button: try sending the lap to the online board again.
lapSummary.post: Button: send the lap to the online board.
lapSummary.queued: Badge: the board couldn't be reached; the lap goes up by itself later.
lapSummary.saveGhost: Button: download the lap as a ghost file (a recording to race against).
lapSummary.signInHint: Shown once per device, under the lap toast and in the lap card, on the first lap that goes up to the online board while signed out.
lapSummary.signIn: Button beside that note: opens Settings > Profile and data > Account (the session pauses).
lapSummary.driver: The name the lap went up under. Keep the tags around {name}; they style it. {name}: the driver's name, not translated.
lapSummary.rename: Button: change the driver's name on the board.
lapSummary.chart.title: Chart title: the lowest speed through each corner.
lapSummary.chart.turn: Short corner name, e.g. 'T4' for turn 4. Keep it short.
lapSummary.chart.bar: Screen-reader name of one corner's bar. {name}: corner name, not translated. {speed}, {unit}: lowest speed and km/h or mph. {delta}: the change against the best lap, e.g. '+1.2'. {state}: none (no earlier lap yet), same, faster or slower.
lapSummary.chart.faster: Chart key: faster through the corner than the best lap.
lapSummary.chart.slower: Chart key: slower through the corner than the best lap.
lapSummary.chart.same: Chart key: the same speed as the best lap.
raceResults.dialog: Screen-reader name of the race results panel.
raceResults.dsq: Disqualified, as a short code in the results. Usually kept as DSQ.
raceResults.dnf: Did not finish, as a short code in the results. Usually kept as DNF.
raceResults.running: In the time column: the car is still racing to the flag.
raceResults.lapsDown: In the gap column: how many laps behind the winner, e.g. '+1 lap'.
raceResults.laps: Badge: the race's length in laps.
raceResults.trackLimits: Badge: how many times the player broke the track limits. {count}: a number.
raceResults.provisional: Badge: the results may still change (cars still finishing).
raceResults.table: Screen-reader name of the results table.
raceResults.colGained: Screen-reader name of the +/- column: places gained from the starting grid.
raceResults.colTime: Column heading: the winner's race time, or each other car's gap to the winner.
raceResults.penaltyTitle: Tooltip on a penalty badge. {seconds}: e.g. '5.0'.
raceResults.promptSelect: Button prompt: confirm the highlighted button.
raceResults.backToLobby: Button: back to the online room's lobby.
raceResults.fastestLapIcon: Screen-reader name of the icon marking the race's fastest lap.
raceResults.noChange: Screen-reader text: the same place as on the grid.
raceResults.notKnown: Screen-reader text: places gained can't be worked out.
raceResults.placesGained: Places moved up from the starting grid.
raceResults.placesLost: Places dropped from the starting grid.
raceResults.yourRace: Screen-reader name of the player's own summary.
raceResults.position: The player's finishing position, e.g. 'P3'. P = position.
raceResults.disqualified: Under the position: the player was disqualified.
raceResults.retired: Under the position: the player didn't finish.
raceResults.ofField: Under the position: out of how many cars, e.g. 'of 12'.
raceResults.gridUnknown: Under places gained: the starting position isn't known.
raceResults.started: Under places gained: the starting position, e.g. 'Started P5'.
raceResults.fastestLap: Under a lap time: the fastest lap of the whole race.
raceResults.bestLap: Under a lap time: the player's best lap.
raceResults.lastRaces.gained: Screen-reader column heading: places gained from the grid.
raceResults.lastRaces.dnf: Did not finish. Usually kept as DNF.
raceResults.joinNext: Button: join the next scheduled online race. {countdown}: time until it starts, e.g. '2:30'. Keep the <time></time> tags around it; they style it.
podiumOverlay.label: Screen-reader name of the podium screen after a race.
podiumOverlay.first: First place, in large type over the podium.
podiumOverlay.second: Second place, in large type over the podium.
podiumOverlay.third: Third place, in large type over the podium.
podiumOverlay.skip: Hint: tap or press to skip the podium to the results.
qualifyingHud.clock: Screen-reader name of the qualifying clock.
qualifyingHud.lastLap: Badge: the qualifying time is up; this is the last lap.
qualifyingHud.badge: Badge on the clock during qualifying.
qualifyingHud.finishIt: Once the time is up: the lap under way still counts if the player finishes it.
qualifyingHud.lapDeleted: Once the time is up: the lap under way doesn't count.
qualifyingHud.best: Small label before the best qualifying lap time.
qualifyingHud.grid: Screen-reader name of the qualifying classification shown before the start.
qualifyingHud.noTime: A driver who set no qualifying lap time.
perfReportCard.title: Card title: a report on the game's frame times (performance), to send to the developer.
perfReportCard.description: Card line: what the report holds (how long each frame took this session).
perfReportCard.failed: The copy failed: the browser refused the clipboard.
perfReportCard.copied: Button text after the report was copied.
perfReportCard.saveFile: Button: download the report as a text file.
perfReportCard.saved: Button text after the report was downloaded.
qualityNotice.lowered: Short note while driving: the game lowered the graphics quality to keep the frame rate up.
qualityNotice.floor: Short note while driving: the frame rate is low even at the lowest quality; a 30 frames-per-second cap is in Settings. FPS = frames per second.
multiPageMfd.pages.elecTag: Tab of the in-car multi-function display (MFD): the electronics tuner page (traction control, ABS, brake bias, diff). Very short, capitals, 4-5 letters fit.
multiPageMfd.pages.elecTitle: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the MFD's electronics page.
multiPageMfd.pages.relTag: MFD tab: the relative page, the cars just ahead of and behind the player on the road. Very short, capitals.
multiPageMfd.pages.relTitle: Tooltip of the MFD's relative page: the cars nearest the player on the road with the time gap to each.
multiPageMfd.pages.tyreTag: MFD tab: tyres and brakes page. Very short, capitals.
multiPageMfd.pages.fuelTag: MFD tab: fuel and battery energy page. Very short, capitals.
multiPageMfd.pages.stndTag: MFD tab: race standings (or the driver's own laps in practice). Abbreviation of Standings, very short, capitals.
multiPageMfd.pages.stndTitle: Tooltip of the MFD's standings page: race positions, or the driver's laps outside a race.
multiPageMfd.panel: Screen-reader name of the in-car display. MFD = multi-function display; keep it as MFD. {page}: the open page's name, already translated.
multiPageMfd.pagesLabel: Screen-reader name of the MFD's row of page tabs.
multiPageMfd.pagesHint: Tooltip on the page tabs. D-pad is the controller's direction pad; Ins is the Insert key (keep the key name).
multiPageMfd.open: Button: unfold the in-car display from its one-line pill.
multiPageMfd.fold: Button: fold the in-car display down to a one-line pill.
multiPageMfd.relative.label: Screen-reader name of the list of nearby cars on the MFD's relative page.
multiPageMfd.relative.noCars: Shown on the relative page when no other car is on track.
multiPageMfd.relative.lapsUp: Tiny tag beside a car that is {count} laps ahead of the player in the race (L = laps). Keep it 3-4 characters.
multiPageMfd.relative.lapsDown: Tiny tag beside a car that is {count} laps behind the player in the race (L = laps). Keep it 3-4 characters.
multiPageMfd.relative.ahead: Screen-reader name of an up arrow: this car is ahead of the player on the road.
multiPageMfd.relative.behind: Screen-reader name of a down arrow: this car is behind the player on the road.
multiPageMfd.relative.clear: Folded MFD summary: no car near the player on the road.
multiPageMfd.relative.you: Stands in for the player's 3-letter driver code (like HAM, VER) when they have set none. Capitals, at most 3-4 letters.
multiPageMfd.fuel.ersPerLap: Battery energy used per lap. ERS = energy recovery system; keep it as ERS.
multiPageMfd.fuel.treadPerLap: Tyre tread worn per lap, in percent.
multiPageMfd.fuel.lapsOfFuel: How many laps the fuel on board lasts. {laps}: a decimal such as 12.3, already formatted.
multiPageMfd.fuel.target: Small line under the fuel used per lap: the fuel per lap that reaches the finish. {kg}: a number such as 1.85.
multiPageMfd.fuel.lift: Advice when the car will run out of fuel before the finish: lift off the throttle early to save {kg} kg of fuel per lap.
multiPageMfd.fuel.fuelOk: There is enough fuel to reach the finish.
multiPageMfd.tyres.label: Screen-reader name of the MFD's grid of four tyre corners.
multiPageMfd.standings.label: Screen-reader name of the race standings table on the MFD.
multiPageMfd.standings.fastestLapShort: Tiny tag beside the driver holding the race's fastest lap. FL = fastest lap; 2 letters.
multiPageMfd.standings.lead: In the gap column, for the race leader (no gap to show). Short.
multiPageMfd.standings.lapTimes: Screen-reader name of the table of the driver's own laps (practice).
multiPageMfd.pill.position: Folded MFD summary of the race position, e.g. P3/20. {position}: the player's place; {fieldSize}: number of cars. P = position.
multiPageMfd.pill.laps: Folded MFD summary in practice: how many laps the driver has completed. The English always says 'laps'; give your language's plural forms.
tunerMfdPanel.categories.bias: Tuner tab: brake bias (front/rear braking balance). Very short, capitals, it shares a narrow row with TC and ABS.
tunerMfdPanel.categories.diff: Tuner tab: differential settings. Very short abbreviation, capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.categories.pwr: Tuner tab: power settings (engine map and ERS deploy). Abbreviation of power, very short, capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.tc1.title: Name of the traction control level dial.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.tc1.low: Tooltip on the minus button: a lower traction control level lets the tyres slip more.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.tc1.high: Tooltip on the plus button: a higher traction control level is safer.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.tc2.title: Name of the dial for how hard traction control cuts power. TC = traction control; keep it as TC.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.tc2.low: Tooltip on the minus button: traction control cuts power more smoothly.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.tc2.high: Tooltip on the plus button: traction control cuts power harder.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.abs.title: Name of the ABS level dial. Usually kept as ABS.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.abs.low: Tooltip on the minus button: ABS steps in later.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.abs.high: Tooltip on the plus button: ABS steps in earlier.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.bias.label: Small dial button: brake bias. Very short, capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.bias.title: Name of the brake bias dial: how the braking is shared between front and rear.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.bias.low: Tooltip on the minus button: moves braking towards the rear.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.bias.high: Tooltip on the plus button: moves braking towards the front.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffEntry.label: Small dial button: the differential's setting for corner entry (braking into a corner). Very short, capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffEntry.title: Name of the dial for the differential's locking on corner entry. Diff = differential.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffEntry.low: Tooltip on the minus button: the car turns in more eagerly.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffEntry.high: Tooltip on the plus button: the car is steadier into the corner.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffMid.label: Small dial button: the differential's setting mid-corner. Very short, capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffMid.title: Name of the dial for the differential's locking mid-corner. Diff = differential.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffMid.low: Tooltip on the minus button: the car rotates more mid-corner.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffMid.high: Tooltip on the plus button: the differential stays locked, the car rotates less.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffExit.label: Small dial button: the differential's setting on corner exit (accelerating out). Very short, capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffExit.title: Name of the dial for the differential's locking on corner exit. Diff = differential.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffExit.low: Tooltip on the minus button: the rear is less likely to snap sideways on exit.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.diffExit.high: Tooltip on the plus button: more traction (drive) out of the corner.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.engineMap.label: Small dial button: engine map. Very short, capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.engineMap.title: Name of the engine map dial (how the engine delivers torque).
tunerMfdPanel.dials.engineMap.low: Tooltip on the minus button: a lower map number gives a sharper throttle response.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.engineMap.high: Tooltip on the plus button: a higher map number gives a smoother throttle response.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.ersMode.title: Name of the dial for how the hybrid battery's energy is deployed. ERS = energy recovery system; keep it as ERS.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.ersMode.low: Tooltip on the minus button: charge the battery more.
tunerMfdPanel.dials.ersMode.high: Tooltip on the plus button: deploy more battery power (attack).
tunerMfdPanel.engineMaps.quali: Engine map name: qualifying map, full power. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.engineMaps.race: Engine map name: the race map. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.engineMaps.smooth: Engine map name: smoother torque. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.engineMaps.lean: Engine map name: lean fuel mixture, saves fuel. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.engineMaps.wet: Engine map name: for a wet track, softest torque. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.ersModes.charge: ERS mode name: harvest energy into the battery. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.ersModes.lowSpeed: ERS mode name: deploy only at low speed. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.ersModes.balanced: ERS mode name: deploy and harvest in balance. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.ersModes.race: ERS mode name: the race deploy mode. Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.ersModes.attack: ERS mode name: deploy everything (overtaking). Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.phases.entry: Corner phase the differential is set for: braking into the corner. Short.
tunerMfdPanel.phases.mid: Corner phase the differential is set for: the middle of the corner. Short.
tunerMfdPanel.phases.exit: Corner phase the differential is set for: accelerating out of the corner. Short.
tunerMfdPanel.chips.tc: Status chip: traction control level and cut, e.g. 'TC 5/6'. Keep TC.
tunerMfdPanel.chips.tcOff: Status chip: traction control switched off. Keep TC.
tunerMfdPanel.chips.bias: Status chip: brake bias in percent to the front, e.g. 'BB 56.0'. BB = brake bias; 2 letters.
tunerMfdPanel.hero.off: Big readout of a dial set to 0 (the aid is off). Capitals, short.
tunerMfdPanel.hero.ofMax: Small tag beside a dial's level: out of {max} (always 12). Capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.hero.lock: Small tag beside a differential dial: how far it locks, e.g. '45% LOCK'. Capitals.
tunerMfdPanel.hero.front: Small tag beside the brake bias value (e.g. 56.0): percent of braking at the front. Capitals; starts with %.
tunerMfdPanel.hero.map: Big readout of the engine map number, e.g. 'M2' (M = map). Very short.
tunerMfdPanel.live.cut: Live bar label: how much engine power traction control is cutting right now.
tunerMfdPanel.live.front: Brake bias at the front, e.g. 'F 56.0' (F = front). Very short.
tunerMfdPanel.live.rear: Brake bias at the rear, e.g. 'R 44.0' (R = rear). Very short.
tunerMfdPanel.live.torque: Live label: the engine map's share of full torque, in percent.
tunerMfdPanel.live.battery: Live label: the hybrid battery's charge, in percent.
tunerMfdPanel.previousDialHint: Tooltip. D-pad is the controller's direction pad; ',' is the comma key.
tunerMfdPanel.nextDialHint: Tooltip. D-pad is the controller's direction pad; '.' is the full stop key.
tunerMfdPanel.lower: Screen-reader name of the minus button. {dial}: the dial's name, already translated (e.g. Brake bias).
tunerMfdPanel.lowerHint: Tooltip on the minus button. {hint}: what lowering the dial does, already translated (e.g. More slip). '-' is the minus key.
tunerMfdPanel.raise: Screen-reader name of the plus button. {dial}: the dial's name, already translated.
tunerMfdPanel.raiseHint: Tooltip on the plus button. {hint}: what raising the dial does, already translated (e.g. Safer). '=' is the equals key.
tunerMfdPanel.foldTuner: Button: fold the electronics tuner down to its status chips.
f12026ChannelsPanel.region: Screen-reader name of the engineering telemetry panel (live car data for engineers).
f12026ChannelsPanel.wheelTitle: Tooltip on one wheel's readings. {wheel}: the wheel's abbreviation, already translated (e.g. LF).
f12026ChannelsPanel.slipRatio: Unit after a wheel's slip ratio in percent. SR = slip ratio. Very short.
f12026ChannelsPanel.aeroHeightTitle: Tooltip: the car's ride height as the aerodynamics see it.
f12026ChannelsPanel.aeroHeight: Tiny label, abbreviation of 'aero height' (ride height). Capitals by style; keep it about 8 characters.
f12026ChannelsPanel.aeroBalanceTitle: Tooltip: the share of downforce on the front axle.
f12026ChannelsPanel.aeroBalance: Tiny label, abbreviation of 'aero balance'. Keep it about 8 characters.
f12026ChannelsPanel.lsdTitle: Tooltip: torque the limited-slip differential is locking with.
f12026ChannelsPanel.lsd: Tiny label. LSD = limited-slip differential (keep LSD); lock = its locking torque.
f12026ChannelsPanel.straightModeTitle: Tooltip. Straight Mode is the 2026 Formula 1 low-drag wing mode on straights (official name; keep it if your language's F1 coverage does).
f12026ChannelsPanel.drsTitle: Tooltip. DRS = the drag reduction system (rear wing flap); keep DRS.
f12026ChannelsPanel.xMode: Label for the 2026 Formula 1 low-drag wing mode (X-mode). Usually kept as it is.
f12026ChannelsPanel.drsState.armed: Wing flap state: allowed, will open at the next press or zone.
f12026ChannelsPanel.drsState.zone: Wing flap state: the car is in a zone where it may open.
f12026ChannelsPanel.drsState.off: Wing flap state: closed, not available.
f12026ChannelsPanel.overtakeEarned: Verdict at the detection point: the driver earned Overtake Mode (extra electric power, 2026 F1 rules). Capitals.
f12026ChannelsPanel.overtakeLocked: Verdict at the detection point: Overtake Mode not earned this lap. Capitals.
f12026ChannelsPanel.noVerdict: No Overtake Mode verdict yet this lap. Capitals.
f12026ChannelsPanel.zoneEarned: Verdict at a DRS detection point: the flap may open in the zone ahead. {zone}: the zone's id such as ZONE_1, not translated. Capitals.
f12026ChannelsPanel.zoneLocked: Verdict at a DRS detection point: the flap may not open. {zone}: the zone's id such as ZONE_1, not translated. Capitals.
f12026ChannelsPanel.noDetection: No DRS detection point passed yet. Capitals.
f12026ChannelsPanel.wall: Warning badge: the car is touching a wall.
f12026ChannelsPanel.aidIntervening: Screen-reader name of a driver-aid lamp while the aid acts. {aid}: TC (traction control) or ABS, not translated.
touchControls.steering: Screen-reader name of the on-screen steering slider (phone controls).
touchControls.drive: Screen-reader name of the phone button that puts an automatic car into drive (shown as D).
touchControls.reverse: Screen-reader name of the phone button that selects reverse gear (shown as R).
touchControls.boost: Screen-reader name of the phone button for the hybrid power boost.
touchControls.activeAero: Screen-reader name of the phone button that opens the movable wing flap (DRS or X-mode).
touchControls.brake: Screen-reader name of the on-screen brake pedal.
touchControls.throttle: Screen-reader name of the on-screen throttle (accelerator) pedal.
touchControls.pause: Screen-reader name of the phone's pause button.
touchControls.camera: Screen-reader name of the phone button that switches camera views.
touchControls.recentreTilt: Screen-reader name: take the phone's current angle as straight ahead for tilt steering.
touchControls.allowMotion: Note while the phone asks for permission to read its motion sensor (tilt steering). Short, it sits between the pedals.
touchControls.tapForTilt: Note: tap the screen to switch tilt steering on. Short.
touchControls.tiltBlocked: Tappable note: the browser refused the motion sensor; tap to ask again. Short.
touchControls.noTiltSensor: Note: this device has no motion sensor, so the steering slider is used instead. Short.
replayBar.region: Screen-reader name of the replay's control bar (play, seek, speed, camera).
replayBar.transport: Screen-reader name of the play / pause and frame-step buttons, as on a video player.
replayBar.previousFrameTitle: Tooltip. {key}: the keyboard key, not translated.
replayBar.playPauseTitle: Tooltip of the replay's play / pause button while flying the free camera.
replayBar.playPauseTitleKey: Tooltip. {key}: the keyboard key's name (Space), not translated.
replayBar.nextFrameTitle: Tooltip. {key}: the keyboard key, not translated.
replayBar.jumpToLap: Tooltip of a lap marker over the replay timeline. {lap}: lap number.
replayBar.lapMarker: Small lap marker button over the replay timeline: L plus the lap number (L3 = lap 3). Keep it very short.
replayBar.timeline: Screen-reader name of the replay's seek slider.
replayBar.timelineValue: Screen-reader value of the seek slider. {elapsed} and {duration}: times such as 1:04.2 or 12.5 s.
replayBar.focusedCar: Screen-reader name of the buttons that pick which car the replay camera follows.
replayBar.switchCarTitle: Tooltip of the button with the followed car's code. {key}: keyboard key, not translated.
replayBar.cycleCamera: Tooltip of the button that steps to the next replay camera.
replayBar.flashbackTitle: Tooltip of the Flashback button: leave the replay and drive on from the moment shown. {key}: keyboard key, not translated. The lap being driven no longer counts.
replayBar.flashback: Button: leave the replay and drive on from the moment shown (rewind). Keep it short.
replayBar.hints.freeCam: Key hints shown while flying the free camera. WASD, Q/E and R are keyboard keys, not translated. Drag = drag the mouse, Scroll = mouse wheel.
replayBar.hints.playPause: Key hint next to the Space key.
replayBar.hints.seek: Key hint next to the left / right arrow keys: jump back or forward. {seconds}: a number of seconds.
replayBar.hints.step: Key hint next to the , and . keys: move one frame back or forward.
replayBar.hints.switchCar: Key hint next to the Tab key: follow another car.
replayBar.hints.freeCamKey: Key hint next to the free camera key: a camera you fly around freely.
replayBar.hints.flashback: Key hint next to the F key: drive on from the moment shown.
timingPanels.tower.region: Screen-reader name of the race order list (timing tower).
timingPanels.tower.lap: Header of the race order. {lap}: current lap number.
timingPanels.tower.lapOf: Header of the race order. {lap}: current lap, {total}: race laps. Keep the <dim></dim> tags around /{total}; they dim it.
timingPanels.tower.driver: Column heading of the race order: the driver's three-letter code.
timingPanels.tower.gap: Column heading: time behind the leader.
timingPanels.tower.interval: Column heading: time behind the car directly ahead.
timingPanels.tower.lastVsYouTitle: Tooltip of the last column: each rival's last lap compared with yours; on your own row, your last lap compared with your best.
timingPanels.tower.lastVsYou:
Two-line column heading (keep the

tag: it is the line break). Their last lap time compared with yours. Very narrow column.
timingPanels.tower.fastestLap: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the purple FL badge: this driver set the fastest lap of the race.
timingPanels.tower.fastestLapShort: Tiny badge: short for Fastest Lap. Two letters at most.
timingPanels.tower.finished: Screen-reader name of the chequered flag icon: this car has finished the race.
timingPanels.tower.damagedTitle: Tooltip of the damage icon. {percent}: damage as a whole number (e.g. 40).
timingPanels.tower.damagedLabel: Screen-reader name of the damage icon. {percent}: damage as a whole number.
timingPanels.tower.out: Shown in the gap column for a car that retired from the race.
timingPanels.tower.leader: Shown in the gap column on the first car when the column shows the gap to the leader.
timingPanels.tower.lead: Shown in the interval column on the first car (it leads the race). Very short.
timingPanels.tower.lastVsBestTitle: Tooltip on your own row's last column.
timingPanels.tower.lastVsTheirsTitle: Tooltip on a rival's last column.
timingPanels.tower.personalBest: Tiny label: PB = personal best (your last lap was your best). Two letters at most.
timingPanels.lap.region: Screen-reader name of the lap timer panel.
timingPanels.lap.outLap: Lap counter on the lap before the first timed lap (driving out of the pits or to the start). Shown in capitals.
timingPanels.lap.counter: Lap counter. {lap}: lap number. {kind} is run on a hill climb or other point-to-point course (one timed run from start to finish), else lap. Shown in capitals.
timingPanels.lap.sector: Sector label: S plus the sector number (S1, S2, S3). A sector is one of the three timed parts of a lap. Keep it very short.
timingPanels.lap.last: Small label before the last lap time.
timingPanels.lap.best: Small label before the best lap time.
timingPanels.lap.noRefLap: No lap time yet to compare the running lap against (ref = reference). Small capitals label.
timingPanels.lap.lastLap: Small label over the last lap time.
timingPanels.lap.bestLap: Small label over the best lap time.
timingPanels.challenge.region: Screen-reader name of the weekly challenge's target panel.
timingPanels.challenge.yourBest: Label over your best lap time in this week's challenge.
timingPanels.challenge.weekFastest: Label over the fastest lap anyone set in this week's challenge.
raceIncidentFeed.calls.investigation: Badge on a race control message: an incident is being investigated.
raceIncidentFeed.calls.penalty: Badge on a race control message: a penalty was given.
raceIncidentFeed.calls.noAction: Badge on a race control message: an incident was reviewed and no further action is taken.
raceIncidentFeed.calls.out: Badge on a race control message: a car has retired from the race.
raceIncidentFeed.calls.raceControl: Badge on a general message from race control (the race officials).
raceIncidentFeed.calls.yellow: Badge on a race control message: yellow flag (danger, slow down).
raceIncidentFeed.calls.green: Badge on a race control message: green flag (track clear).
raceIncidentFeed.calls.warning: Badge on a race control message: a warning to a driver.
raceIncidentFeed.vsc.tag: VSC = Virtual Safety Car: every car must slow to a set pace. Keep VSC if your language uses the abbreviation.
raceIncidentFeed.vsc.ending: The Virtual Safety Car period is about to end.
raceIncidentFeed.vsc.slowDown: Under the Virtual Safety Car: you are too fast, slow down.
raceIncidentFeed.vsc.slowToTarget: Under the Virtual Safety Car: slow to the target pace (you still have a few seconds to do it).
raceIncidentFeed.vsc.prepareForGreen: The Virtual Safety Car is ending: get ready for racing to resume.
raceIncidentFeed.vsc.noOvertaking: Under the Virtual Safety Car: overtaking is not allowed.
raceIncidentFeed.flag.yieldNow: Blue flag, after a warning: a faster car is lapping you. {code}: its three-letter driver code.
raceIncidentFeed.flag.letThrough: Blue flag: a faster car is lapping you, let it pass. {code}: its three-letter driver code.
raceIncidentFeed.flag.doubleYellowCue: Under double yellow flags (serious danger ahead).
raceIncidentFeed.flag.yellowCue: Under a yellow flag (danger ahead): overtaking is not allowed.
raceIncidentFeed.flag.blue: Flag tag: blue flag (a faster car is lapping you).
raceControlBanner.decisions.warning: Track limits decision badge: a warning for leaving the track.
raceControlBanner.decisions.finalWarning: Track limits decision badge: the last warning before a penalty (black-and-white flag).
raceControlBanner.decisions.penalty: Track limits decision badge: a time penalty.
raceControlBanner.decisions.disqualified: Track limits decision badge: the driver is disqualified.
raceControlBanner.decisions.lapInvalid: Track limits decision badge: the lap time doesn't count.
raceControlBanner.decisions.cleared: Track limits decision badge: the advantage was given back, nothing more to do.
raceControlBanner.decisions.noAdvantage: Track limits decision badge: no advantage was gained, no further action.
raceControlBanner.warningsMeter: Screen-reader text of the warning dots. {count}: warnings so far, {total}: warnings before a penalty.
raceControlBanner.pointsMeter: Screen-reader text of the track limits points meter. {points}: points so far (e.g. 1.25), {allowed}: points allowed before a penalty.
raceControlBanner.giveBack.toCar: You overtook under yellow flags: give the place back to this car. P = position. {code}: the car's three-letter driver code.
raceControlBanner.giveBack.dropTo: You gained a place illegally: drop back to this position. {position}: a position number (P3 = third place).
raceControlBanner.giveBack.time: You gained time by leaving the track: give that time back. {seconds}: seconds, e.g. 0.42.
raceControlBanner.giveBack.slowDown: You gained an advantage by leaving the track: slow down to give it back.
raceControlBanner.giveBack.underYellow: Badge: you overtook a car under yellow flags (not allowed).
raceControlBanner.giveBack.illegalOverta: Badge: you overtook a car by leaving the track.
raceControlBanner.giveBack.trackLimits: Badge: you gained time by leaving the track (track limits).
raceControlBanner.offTrack.trackLimits: Banner title while the car is off the track: the track limits rules are watching.
raceControlBanner.offTrack.offTrack: The car is off the track right now.
raceControlBanner.offTrack.underReview: The car is back on track; the excursion is being reviewed by race control.
startLights.startsIn: Countdown before the start lights. {seconds}: whole seconds left. Keep the <n></n> tags around the number; they style it.
startLights.lightsLabel: Screen-reader text of the five red start lights. {lit}: lights on, {total}: always 5.
startLights.rollingStart: Badge: a rolling start (the field drives to the start line at a set pace instead of starting from a standstill).
startLights.holdPaceSkin: Rolling start instruction. {pace}: the pace speed, {unit}: km/h or mph (not translated). Keep the <n></n> tags around the number. Start/finish = the start-finish line.
startLights.holdPace: Rolling start instruction, shorter form. {pace}: the pace speed, {unit}: km/h or mph (not translated). Keep the <n></n> tags. Line = the start line.
startLights.greenFlag: Big banner when a rolling start goes green (the race starts).
startLights.lightsOut: Big banner when the start lights go out (the race starts).
startLights.chequeredFlag: Big banner when you finish the race.
launchCue.stalledLabel: Screen-reader text when the engine has stalled. {control}: the clutch button or key, or the word for clutch.
launchCue.clutch: The clutch pedal, as the thing to hold (used inside 'hold ...' when no button is mapped). Lower case.
launchCue.stalled: Shown in capitals when the engine stalls. <control></control> is replaced by the clutch button glyph or its name. N = neutral gear, keep it as N.
launchCue.jumpStart: You moved before the lights went out. {seconds}: the time penalty in seconds.
launchCue.manualStart: Screen-reader text of the manual start checklist. The clutch part: held = the clutch is held in. The revs part: up = the engine revs are high enough to launch.
launchCue.holdNamed: Manual start step, in capitals. {control}: the name of the control mapped as clutch (e.g. a paddle), not translated.
launchCue.holdClutch: Manual start step, in capitals: hold the clutch in.
launchCue.revsUp: Manual start step, in capitals: raise the engine revs to the launch range.
speedCluster.region: Screen-reader name of the dash with speed, gear and rev lights.
speedCluster.minimalRegion: Screen-reader name of the small speed and gear box.
speedCluster.shiftLights: Screen-reader text of the rev lights. {lit}: lights on, {total}: lights in the strip.
speedCluster.gearLabel: Screen-reader text. {gear}: the gear (1-8, N for neutral, R for reverse).
speedCluster.gear: Small label over the gear number.
speedCluster.shift: Badge: change up a gear now (the revs are at the shift point).
speedCluster.aeroToggle: Screen-reader name of the aero button. {label}: the wing state such as DRS OPEN or X-MODE, not translated here.
speedCluster.drsTitle: Tooltip. DRS = drag reduction system, keep it. {key}: keyboard key. Detection point = the line where the gap to the car ahead is measured.
speedCluster.straightModeTitle: Tooltip. Straight Mode is the 2026 cars' low-drag wing mode on straights. {key}: keyboard key.
speedCluster.overtakeLockedTitle: Tooltip. Overtake Mode is the 2026 cars' extra electric power for overtaking. {keys}: keyboard key and pad button, not translated.
speedCluster.overtakeTitle: Tooltip. {keys}: keyboard key and pad button, not translated.
speedCluster.boostTitle: Tooltip: the extra electric power button. {keys}: keyboard key and pad button, not translated.
speedCluster.overtake: Button badge: Overtake Mode (2026 cars' extra electric power). Short.
speedCluster.boost: Button badge: extra electric power. Short.
speedCluster.harvest: Battery label: the hybrid system is recharging the battery under braking. Short capitals label.
speedCluster.deploy: Battery label: the hybrid system is using the battery's power. Short capitals label.
speedCluster.ersSoc: Battery label. ERS = energy recovery system (keep it), SOC = state of charge. Short capitals label.
speedCluster.lonG: Short capitals label: longitudinal g-force (braking and accelerating). G = g-force.
speedCluster.inputs: Screen-reader name of the three pedal / steering force bars.
speedCluster.brakeLetter: One letter under the brake pedal bar (B = brake).
speedCluster.throttleLetter: One letter under the throttle pedal bar (T = throttle).
speedCluster.forceLetter: One letter under the steering force bar (F = force feedback).
speedCluster.clip: Replaces the F under the steering force bar when force feedback clips (is cut off at its maximum). Up to four letters.
speedCluster.forceTitle: Tooltip of the steering force bar. Clipping = the force is cut off at the wheel's maximum.
speedCluster.latG: Lateral (sideways) g-force. {g}: a number such as 2.4. g is the unit; lat = lateral.
speedCluster.ersBattery: Tooltip of the battery bar. ERS = energy recovery system, keep it.
speedCluster.rpmBand: Tooltip of the engine revs bar (RPM = revolutions per minute, keep it).
hudFormat.session.qualifying: Session name on the driving HUD: a timed qualifying session.
hudFormat.session.timeTrial: Session name on the driving HUD: the weekly challenge's time trial.
hudFormat.session.practice: Session name on the driving HUD: driving alone, untimed practice.
hudFormat.cornerShort: Short corner number on the circuit map caption, e.g. T4 = turn 4. {turn}: the corner's number. Keep it very short.
hudFormat.lapMark.best: How a sector or lap time went: the fastest of the session. Read out by screen readers and shown in tooltips.
hudFormat.lapMark.pb: How a sector or lap time went: the player's own best, but not the session's best.
hudFormat.lapMark.slower: How a sector or lap time went: slower than the best.
thirdPartyData.you: The player's own name in a timing list during an online race.
thirdPartyData.headlight.flash: Headlights state on the HUD's weather panel: the player is flashing the high beams.
thirdPartyData.headlight.on: Headlights state on the HUD's weather panel: switched on.
thirdPartyData.headlight.off: Headlights state on the HUD's weather panel: switched off by hand.
thirdPartyData.surface.dry: Track surface state on the HUD's weather panel.
thirdPartyData.surface.damp: Track surface state on the HUD's weather panel: slightly wet.
thirdPartyData.surface.wet: Track surface state on the HUD's weather panel.
thirdPartyData.surface.flooded: Track surface state on the HUD's weather panel: standing water.
aeroLabel.readout.noDrs: Dash badge, in capitals: the car's era has no DRS (drag reduction system, the opening rear wing flap). Keep DRS as is.
aeroLabel.readout.drsOpen: Dash badge, in capitals: the DRS flap is open.
aeroLabel.readout.drsQueued: Dash badge, in capitals: the player pressed the DRS button early; the flap opens when the zone starts.
aeroLabel.readout.drsArmed: Dash badge, in capitals: DRS may be opened here (the car is in a zone it earned).
aeroLabel.readout.xMode: Dash badge, in capitals: the 2026 low-drag aero mode with the wing flaps open. X-MODE is the rule's own name; keep it unless your language's broadcasts translate it.
aeroLabel.readout.xQueued: Dash badge, in capitals: the player pressed the X-mode button early; the flaps open on the next straight. X = X-mode.
aeroLabel.readout.xArmed: Dash badge, in capitals: X-mode may be opened here. X = X-mode.
aeroLabel.readout.zMode: Dash badge, in capitals: the 2026 high-downforce aero mode for corners (flaps shut). Z-MODE is the rule's own name; keep it unless your language's broadcasts translate it.
aeroLabel.notice.drsEnabled: Race-control notice at a DRS detection point: the car was within a second of the car ahead, so it may open DRS in the next zone.
aeroLabel.notice.drsNotEnabled: Race-control notice at a DRS detection point: the car may not open DRS in the next zone.
aeroLabel.notice.drsQueued: Race-control notice beside a DRS badge: a press of the button is kept and the flap opens when the zone starts.
aeroLabel.notice.xModeBadge: Badge on the 2026 race-control notice, in capitals: the X-mode aero mode. Keep it as the dash's X-MODE.
aeroLabel.notice.straightMode: 2026 notice: a straight where every car may open its wing flaps (Straight Mode, the rule's own name) is coming up.
aeroLabel.notice.xModeQueued: 2026 notice beside the X-MODE badge: a press of the button is kept and the flaps open on the next straight.
aeroLabel.notice.overtakeBadge: Badge on the 2026 race-control notice, in capitals: Overtake Mode, an extra burst of electric power the car earns by being within a second of the car ahead.
aeroLabel.notice.overtakeEnabled: Beside the OVERTAKE badge: the car earned Overtake Mode for this lap.
aeroLabel.notice.overtakeLocked: Beside the OVERTAKE badge: the car did not earn Overtake Mode.
tyreBrakeWidget.corner.fl: Tyre position, abbreviated: front left. Keep it two letters if you can.
tyreBrakeWidget.tread.inner: One letter under the tyre drawing: the inner tread band.
tyreBrakeWidget.tread.middle: One letter under the tyre drawing: the middle tread band.
tyreBrakeWidget.tread.outer: One letter under the tyre drawing: the outer tread band.
tyreBrakeWidget.tread.title: Tooltip on the three letters under the tyre drawing.
tyreBrakeWidget.condition.grain: Short badge on a tyre: graining (the tread surface tearing into rolls of rubber).
tyreBrakeWidget.condition.blister: Short badge on a tyre: blistering (bubbles from an overheated core).
tyreBrakeWidget.condition.flat: Short badge on a tyre: a flat spot worn by a locked wheel.
tyreBrakeWidget.condition.dirt: Short badge on a tyre: dirt and rubber marbles picked up off the racing line.
tyreBrakeWidget.conditionTitle: Tooltip on a tyre condition badge. {title}: the condition's description, already translated. {level}: how bad, 0 to 100.
tyreBrakeWidget.brakeTitle: Tooltip on the brake disc bar. {disc} and {core}: temperatures with their unit (e.g. 650°C). The core part shows when {hasCore} is yes. {bite}: how much the pads still grip, in percent, shown when {hasBite} is yes.
tyreBrakeWidget.cardTitle: Tooltip on a tyre card. {corner}: the tyre position (FL, FR, RL, RR), already translated. {temps}: three temperatures, outer to inner, e.g. '92° / 95° / 98°'.
tyreBrakeWidget.treadLife: Tooltip on the percentage of tread left on a tyre.
tyreBrakeWidget.pressureTitle: Tooltip on the tyre pressure. {unit}: bar or psi.
tyreBrakeWidget.windowTitle: Tooltip on the temperature range the tyre works best in.
tyreBrakeWidget.window: Short label before the tyres' best temperature range, e.g. 'Window 85°–105°C'.
tyreBrakeWidget.miniTitle: Tooltip on a small tyre readout. {corner}: tyre position, already translated. {temps}: three temperatures. {pressure}: e.g. '27.5 psi', or '--' when unknown. {brake}: brake temperature. {condition}: the worst condition's name, shown when {hasCondition} is yes.
tyrePanel.region: Screen-reader name of the tyre and brake temperatures panel.
weatherBadge.region: Screen-reader name of the weather readout on the driving HUD.
weatherBadge.air: Short label before the air temperature.
weatherBadge.track: Short label before the track surface temperature.
weatherBadge.wind: Short label before the wind speed, when the wind's direction is unknown.
weatherBadge.headlightsForcedOn: Screen-reader name of the headlights icon: the player switched them on by hand.
weatherBadge.headlightsForcedOff: Screen-reader name of the headlights icon: the player switched them off by hand.
weatherBadge.headlightsOn: Screen-reader name of the headlights icon: on automatically.
weatherBadge.headlightsTitleAuto: Tooltip: the headlights came on by themselves (automatic mode).
weatherBadge.chipFlash: Tiny chip beside the headlights icon, in capitals: the player is flashing the high beams.
weatherBadge.chipOn: Tiny chip beside the headlights icon, in capitals: switched on by hand.
weatherBadge.chipOff: Tiny chip beside the headlights icon, in capitals: switched off by hand.
damageWidget.label: Label above the car damage percentage.
damageWidget.out: Shown instead of the damage percentage: the car is too damaged to go on (retired).
damageWidget.title: Tooltip on the damage drawing. Each value is a percentage of damage on that side of the car, e.g. '35%'.
damageWidget.titlePunctured: As the damage tooltip, with a punctured tyre.
damageWidget.part.floor: The worst-damaged part of the car: the floor and sidepods.
inputTrace.throttle: Very short legend of the throttle trace (abbreviation of Throttle), shown in capitals.
inputTrace.brake: Very short legend of the brake trace (abbreviation of Brake), shown in capitals.
inputTrace.steering: Very short legend of the steering trace (abbreviation of Steering), shown in capitals.
inputTrace.steeringTitle: Tooltip on the steering legend: the solid line is the road wheels' angle, the dashed line the player's input.
inputTrace.trace: Screen-reader description of the live chart of throttle, brake and steering.
inputTrace.region: Screen-reader name of the inputs panel (pedals and steering).
pedalBars.region: Screen-reader name of the pedal bars and the electronic aids (ABS, TC) acting on them.
pedalBars.clutch: Very short label under the clutch pedal bar (abbreviation of Clutch).
pedalBars.clip: Short label under the force feedback bar while the wheel's force is clipping (asked for more than the motor gives).
pedalBars.steering: Screen-reader name of the steering bar.
splitGaps.region: Screen-reader name of the gaps to the cars directly ahead and behind.
splitGaps.ahead: Short label: the car directly ahead in the race.
splitGaps.behind: Short label: the car directly behind in the race.
splitGaps.carAhead: Screen-reader text. {driver}: a three-letter driver code. {gap}: seconds between the cars, e.g. 1.234.
splitGaps.carBehind: Screen-reader text. {driver}: a three-letter driver code. {gap}: seconds between the cars, e.g. 1.234.
splitGaps.goingYourWay: Arrow meaning: the gap moved in the player's favour.
splitGaps.goingAgainstYou: Arrow meaning: the gap moved against the player.
splitGaps.steady: Arrow meaning: the gap held steady.
deltaBar.label: Screen-reader name of the bar showing time gained or lost against the reference lap.
deltaBar.valueText: Screen-reader value of the delta bar. {delta}: signed seconds, e.g. −0.234. The trend says whether time is being gained, lost or held.
deltaBar.noReference: Screen-reader value of the delta bar before there is a lap to compare with.
ffbMeter.title: Panel title and its screen-reader name: the steering wheel's force feedback.
ffbMeter.clipping: Badge: the wheel's force is clipping (asking for more than the motor gives).
ffbMeter.inRange: Badge: the wheel's force is within what the motor gives.
ffbMeter.peak: Recent highest force. {value}: a percentage number. Keep the <v></v> tags around the value; they style it.
ffbMeter.setCar: Button: set this car's force feedback strength. {value}: a percentage number.
proximityRadar.carsClose: Screen-reader text of the radar around the player's car. The side part says whether a car is right beside the player on the left, the right, both or neither.
proximityRadar.clear: Screen-reader text: no cars near the player.
cameraToast.freeHintTouch: Hint under the free camera's name on a touch screen. Pause and Replay are the game's own menus.
cameraToast.freeHintKeys: Hint under the free camera's name: mouse drag looks around, WASD keys fly, Q/E change height, the scroll wheel sets speed, R resets. WASD, Q/E and R are keyboard keys: keep them. {key}: the key that leaves the free camera, e.g. F7.
ffbPairPrompt.region: Screen-reader name of the prompt to pair a steering wheel for force feedback.
ffbPairPrompt.text: Prompt: connect the steering wheel through the browser so the game can drive its force feedback.
dualSensePairPrompt.text: Prompt when a PlayStation DualSense controller is seen. Keep the tags around the first part; they bold it. Pairing lets the game drive the adaptive triggers and haptics.
dualSensePairPrompt.dismiss: Button: close the prompt for good.
overheadNameplates.fastestLap: Tiny chip on the name floating above a car: this driver set the fastest lap. Abbreviation of Fastest lap.
overheadNameplates.rank: Place in the order on the name floating above a car, e.g. P3 = third. {rank}: the place number.
hiddenNote.off: Banner while the player has hidden the HUD.
hiddenNote.offKey: The same banner with the key or button that shows the HUD again. {key}: a key or button name, untranslated.
startLights.reaction: Pill under the 'Lights out' banner: how long the player took to launch after the lights went out. <n> wraps the number ({ms}, whole milliseconds); keep 'ms'.
hudEditor.title: Title of the live HUD layout editor (Settings > Display > HUD > Edit layout), shown over the game.
hudEditor.hint: One-line instructions in the editor's bar: drag a panel to move it; drag its corner handle or use the mouse wheel over it to make it bigger or smaller.
hudEditor.parts.top-left: Name tab on the frame around the HUD's top-left group of panels (what is in it depends on the HUD design).
hudEditor.parts.top-center: Name tab on the frame around the HUD's top-centre group (start lights, delta bar).
hudEditor.parts.top-right: Name tab on the frame around the HUD's top-right group (usually the circuit map).
hudEditor.parts.center-right: Name tab on the frame around the manual start's checklist on the right edge (hold the clutch, revs).
hudEditor.parts.center: Name tab on the frame around the proximity radar in the middle of the screen.
hudEditor.parts.bottom-left: Name tab on the frame around the HUD's bottom-left group (usually tyres).
hudEditor.parts.bottom-center: Name tab on the frame around the HUD's bottom-centre group (speed, gear, revs).
hudEditor.parts.bottom-right: Name tab on the frame around the HUD's bottom-right group (usually the MFD).
hudEditor.resetPart: Small button on one moved panel's frame: puts that panel back where the design puts it.
hudEditor.resize: Tooltip on the corner handle that resizes a panel.
hudEditor.resetAll: Button in the editor's bar: puts every panel of this HUD design back.
hudEditor.cancel: Button in the editor's bar: closes it and drops the changes made in it.
hudEditor.done: Button in the editor's bar: closes it and keeps the changes.
speedCluster.lowGrip: Badge where the Overtake button sits once race control declares Low Grip Conditions (a wet track) under F1's 2026 rules. Short.
speedCluster.overtakeAuto: Badge while the game's Automatic Overtake setting is using the car's Overtake. Short.
speedCluster.overtake2026LockedTitle: Tooltip. The detection line and activation line are painted lines on the track in F1's 2026 rules.
touchControls.overtakeShort: Two-letter abbreviation of Overtake on a small round touch button; keep it two or three letters.
leaderboardPanel.viewLabel: Screen-reader name of the switch between Lap times and Telemetry inside the Lap times panel.
leaderboardPanel.tabTimes: Tab label showing the online and local lap time tables.
leaderboardPanel.tabAnalysis: Tab label showing the lap telemetry comparison charts.
leaderboardPanel.analysisEmpty: Empty state shown on the Telemetry tab before any lap has been completed for this car and circuit.
lapSummary.analyzeLap: Button on the post-lap card that opens the lap telemetry comparison modal.
lapTelemetry.title: Heading of the lap telemetry comparison panel and modal.
lapTelemetry.description: Subtitle explaining that the dashed trace is the reference lap, the solid trace is the compared lap, and hovering scrubs the cursor.
lapTelemetry.reference: Label for the baseline lap being compared against (dashed trace).
lapTelemetry.compared: Label for the target lap being compared (solid trace).
lapTelemetry.allTimeBest: Option name in the lap picker for the driver's personal best lap in this car on this circuit.
lapTelemetry.latestLap: Option name in the lap picker for the most recent persisted lap.
lapTelemetry.sessionLap: Option name in the lap picker for a lap driven in the current session. {lap}: lap number.
lapTelemetry.invalidTag: Short tag appended to a lap in the picker when it broke track limits or used autopilot.
lapTelemetry.channels.brake: Telemetry chart title: brake pedal application.
lapTelemetry.channels.throttle: Telemetry chart title: throttle pedal application.
lapTelemetry.channels.delta: Telemetry chart title: cumulative time difference against the reference lap.
lapTelemetry.units.gear: Short unit symbol for gear number.
lapTelemetry.units.seconds: Short unit abbreviation for seconds (e.g. s).
lapTelemetry.drivingLine: Heading for the circuit driving-line map coloured by time gained or lost.
lapTelemetry.startFinish: Short marker label for the start/finish line on the driving-line map.
lapTelemetry.legend.fastest: Map key: strongest time-gain segment on the lap.
lapTelemetry.legend.faster: Map key: faster than the reference lap.
lapTelemetry.legend.same: Map key: roughly the same pace as the reference lap.
lapTelemetry.legend.slower: Map key: slower than the reference lap.
lapTelemetry.sectors: Heading for the three-sector delta breakdown.
lapTelemetry.sectorShort: Short sector label, e.g. S1, S2, S3. {sector}: 1-3.
lapTelemetry.sectorSplit: Distance axis label for a sector boundary. {sector}: 1 or 2; {distance}: formatted distance with unit.
lapTelemetry.cursorAt: Live scrub readout showing the cursor's distance along the lap. {distance}: formatted distance with unit.
lapTelemetry.insights: Heading for the automatic sector and corner observations.
lapTelemetry.noInsights: Shown when the compared laps have no notable sector or corner differences.
lapTelemetry.insight.sectorLossTitle: Observation title: largest sector time loss. {sector}: 1-3.
lapTelemetry.insight.sectorLossDetail: Observation text: time lost in that sector. {seconds}: formatted decimal; {sector}: 1-3.
lapTelemetry.insight.sectorGainTitle: Observation title: largest sector time gain. {sector}: 1-3.
lapTelemetry.insight.sectorGainDetail: Observation text: time gained in that sector. {seconds}: formatted decimal; {sector}: 1-3.
lapTelemetry.insight.apexTitle: Observation title for a corner without a proper name. {turn}: corner number.
lapTelemetry.insight.apexNamedTitle: Observation title for a named corner. {turn}: corner number; {name}: corner name (untranslated).
lapTelemetry.insight.apexFasterDetail: Observation text: higher minimum speed through the corner. {speed}: whole number; {unit}: km/h or mph; {turn}: corner number.
lapTelemetry.insight.apexSlowerDetail: Observation text: lower minimum speed through the corner. {speed}: whole number; {unit}: km/h or mph; {turn}: corner number.
lapTelemetry.insight.brakeTitle: Observation title for a corner braking point without a proper name. {turn}: corner number.
lapTelemetry.insight.brakeNamedTitle: Observation title for a named corner braking point. {turn}: corner number; {name}: corner name (untranslated).
lapTelemetry.insight.brakeEarlierDetail: Observation text: braked earlier approaching the corner. {distance}: whole number; {unit}: m or ft; {turn}: corner number.
lapTelemetry.insight.brakeLaterDetail: Observation text: braked later approaching the corner. {distance}: whole number; {unit}: m or ft; {turn}: corner number.
